# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

This includes technologies such as IBM i, IBM Z, z/OS, Db2, CICS, COBOL, JCL, RPG, AIX, and watsonx, even when the user does not explicitly say IBM.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

arguments.content:
# FlakeHunter — Hackathon Plan

## Goal
A one-day CLI tool that finds flaky tests in a Python/pytest project, diagnoses them, auto-patches them via IBM Bob, and proves the fix. Outputs a Markdown report, an HTML report, and per-patch `.diff` files.

---

## Project Structure

```
FlakeHunter/
├── demo_app/
│   ├── app.py                  # tiny sample app (counter, fetch, random picker)
│   └── tests/
│       ├── test_stable.py      # ~8-10 always-passing tests
│       ├── test_flaky_sleep.py # flaky: timing / time.sleep race
│       ├── test_flaky_random.py# flaky: random without seed
│       ├── test_flaky_network.py # flaky: real network call (httpbin / socket)
│       └── test_flaky_state.py # flaky: shared global/module-level state
│
├── flakehunter/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── cli.py                  # entry point — Click CLI
│   ├── runner.py               # re-run detection (subprocess pytest, N passes)
│   ├── scanner.py              # static hint scanner (AST walk, ~50 lines)
│   ├── diagnoser.py            # parallel Bob subprocesses, one per flaky test
│   ├── patcher.py              # apply patch, verify 50/50, revert or keep
│   └── reporter.py             # Markdown + self-contained HTML report
│
├── reports/                    # created at runtime
│   ├── report.md
│   ├── report.html
│   └── <test_name>.diff        # one per attempted patch
│
├── requirements.txt
├── pyproject.toml              # [project.scripts] flakehunter = "flakehunter.cli:main"
└── PLAN.md                     # this file
```

---

## Part 1 — demo_app/

### `app.py`
Three tiny functions used by the tests:
- `increment(counter_dict)` — mutates a shared dict (enables shared-state flakiness)
- `random_winner(items)` — returns `random.choice(items)` (no seed)
- `fetch_status(url)` — does a real `urllib.request.urlopen(url).status` call

### `tests/test_stable.py` (~8-10 tests)
Pure, deterministic tests: arithmetic, string ops, list ops, dict ops. Always pass. Exist to prove FlakeHunter doesn't false-positive on good tests.

### `tests/test_flaky_sleep.py` (1 test)
Hint category: **timing**
```python
# Records a start time, sleeps a variable amount, asserts elapsed < threshold.
# Flaky because the sleep can overrun on a loaded CI machine.
```

### `tests/test_flaky_random.py` (1 test)
Hint category: **random**
```python
# Calls random_winner() and asserts a specific element is returned.
# Flaky because no seed is set.
```

### `tests/test_flaky_network.py` (1 test)
Hint category: **network**
```python
# Calls fetch_status("http://httpbin.org/status/200") and asserts status == 200.
# Flaky because the network may be down or the host may be slow.
```

### `tests/test_flaky_state.py` (1 test)
Hint category: **shared-state**
```python
# Imports a module-level counter dict and calls increment() without resetting it.
# Flaky when pytest re-uses the module across parametrize or re-runs.
```

---

## Part 2 — flakehunter/

### `cli.py` — Click CLI
```
flakehunter run <project_path>
  --runs        N      # how many re-run passes (default: 10)
  --workers     W      # parallel Bob subprocesses (default: 4)
  --max-cost    $      # per-Bob-call cost cap forwarded to bob --max-cost
  --dry-run            # skip Bob calls; report hints only, no patches
  --output      DIR    # where to write reports/ (default: ./reports)
```
Orchestrates the four phases in order: detect → hint → diagnose → patch → report.

---

### Phase 1 — `runner.py` — Re-run Detection

**Algorithm:**
1. Run `pytest <project_path> --tb=no -q` as a subprocess **N times** (default 10).
2. Collect pass/fail outcome per test node ID on each run (parse `pytest --json-report` or `-v` output).
3. A test is **flaky** if it has at least one PASS and at least one FAIL across the N runs.
4. Return a list of `FlakySummary(node_id, pass_count, fail_count)`.

**Key decisions:**
- Use `pytest-json-report` plugin (add to `requirements.txt`) for reliable machine-readable output.
- Runs are sequential (not parallel) to avoid shared-state tests masking each other.
- All tests are always run — static hints never filter or skip a test.

---

### Phase 2 — `scanner.py` — Static Hint Scanner

**Algorithm:**
1. For each flaky `node_id`, resolve the source file path.
2. `ast.parse()` the file and walk all nodes.
3. Attach hint labels if any of these patterns appear **anywhere in the file**:

| Hint label      | AST pattern to detect                                      |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `timing`        | `time.sleep(...)` call or `import time`                    |
| `random`        | `random.*` call or `import random`                         |
| `network`       | `urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, `socket`, `http` import     |
| `shared-state`  | module-level mutable assignment (list/dict literal at top) |

4. Return `hints: list[str]` per flaky test (may be empty — that's fine).
5. **Hints are advisory only.** They are injected into the Bob prompt to give context. They never gate or skip a test.

**Constraint:** This module should stay under ~60 lines. No external deps.

---

### Phase 3 — `diagnoser.py` — Bob-Powered Diagnosis & Patch Generation

**Algorithm:**
1. Build one prompt per flaky test:
   ```
   You are fixing a flaky pytest test.
   Test: <node_id>
   File: <source_file>
   Hints: <hint labels from scanner>
   Pass rate: <X>/N runs

   Read the test file and the app code it imports.
   Produce a minimal unified diff that makes the test deterministic.
   Output ONLY the unified diff, nothing else.
   ```
2. Spawn one `bob run "<prompt>" --workspace <project_path> --format json --trust --accept-license --max-cost <limit>` subprocess **per flaky test**, all in **parallel** using `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor` (or `ThreadPoolExecutor` with subprocess).
3. Collect stdout from each Bob process. Parse the JSON response to extract the diff text.
4. If `--dry-run` is set, skip all Bob calls and return `None` diff for every test.
5. Return a list of `DiagnosisResult(node_id, diff_text | None, bob_raw_output)`.

---

### Phase 4 — `patcher.py` — Apply, Verify 50/50, Revert or Keep

For each `DiagnosisResult` with a non-None diff:

1. **Save the diff** to `reports/<sanitized_node_id>.diff` unconditionally.
2. **Apply the patch** using Python's `subprocess.run(["patch", "-p1"], input=diff_text)` against the project path.
3. **Verify**: run `pytest <node_id>` exactly **50 times** sequentially.
4. **Decision:**
   - If all 50 runs pass → **keep the patch**. Record `status=fixed`.
   - If any run fails → **revert**: run `patch -p1 -R` to undo the change. Record `status=suggestion_only`.
5. Return a list of `PatchResult(node_id, status, diff_path)`.

**Safety rule:** The original file is always restored on revert. If `patch` itself fails to apply, record `status=patch_failed` and skip verification.

---

### Phase 5 — `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML Report

Generates two files in `<output>/`:

#### `report.md` structure:
```markdown
# FlakeHunter Report
Generated: <timestamp>  Project: <path>  Runs: N

## Summary
| Test | Pass | Fail | Hints | Outcome |
|------|------|------|-------|---------|
| ...  |  8   |  2   | timing, random | ✅ fixed |

## Details
### <test_node_id>
- **Hints:** timing
- **Outcome:** fixed
- **Diff:** [view patch](test_name.diff)
...
```

#### `report.html`
- Single self-contained `.html` file (inline CSS, no external dependencies).
- Same content as the Markdown report but rendered as an HTML table.
- Color-coded rows: green = fixed, yellow = suggestion_only, red = patch_failed, grey = no diff (dry-run).
- Each row has a collapsible `<details>` block showing the raw diff inline.

---

## Data Flow

```
cli.py
  │
  ├─► runner.py        → list[FlakySummary]
  │
  ├─► scanner.py       → dict[node_id → list[str]]  (hints)
  │
  ├─► diagnoser.py     → list[DiagnosisResult]       (parallel Bob subprocesses)
  │
  ├─► patcher.py       → list[PatchResult]            (apply / verify 50x / revert)
  │
  └─► reporter.py      → reports/report.md
                          reports/report.html
                          reports/<test>.diff
```

---

## `requirements.txt`

```
click>=8.1
pytest>=7.0
pytest-json-report>=1.5
```

No other runtime dependencies. `patch` binary must be available on PATH (standard on Linux/macOS; on Windows use Git Bash or WSL).

---

## `pyproject.toml` (minimal)

```toml
[project]
name = "flakehunter"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = ["click>=8.1", "pytest>=7.0", "pytest-json-report>=1.5"]

[project.scripts]
flakehunter = "flakehunter.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools"]
build-backend = "setuptools.backends.legacy:build"
```

---

## One-Day Build Order

| # | Task | Est. |
|---|------|------|
| 1 | Scaffold folders, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt` | 15 min |
| 2 | Write `demo_app/app.py` + all 5 test files | 30 min |
| 3 | `runner.py` — re-run detection loop | 45 min |
| 4 | `scanner.py` — AST hint scanner | 30 min |
| 5 | `cli.py` — Click wiring, `--dry-run` flag | 30 min |
| 6 | `diagnoser.py` — Bob subprocess + parallel executor | 60 min |
| 7 | `patcher.py` — apply/verify/revert loop | 45 min |
| 8 | `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML | 45 min |
| 9 | End-to-end smoke test with `--dry-run` | 20 min |
|10 | End-to-end test with real Bob (credits) | 30 min |
| **Total** | | **~6 hr** |

---

## Key Design Constraints (do not drift from these)

- Static hints **never** gate or skip any test — re-run is always the detection source of truth.
- Bob is called via **subprocess** (`bob run "..." --workspace ... --format json --trust --accept-license --max-cost ...`), one process per flaky test, all in parallel.
- `--dry-run` skips ALL Bob calls; the rest of the pipeline (detect, hint, report) still runs.
- A patch is kept **only if it passes 50/50 sequential re-runs**; otherwise the file is auto-reverted.
- Every attempted diff is saved to `reports/<test>.diff` regardless of outcome.
- HTML report is **self-contained** (no CDN links, no external CSS).

---

### The 5 Phases

| Phase | Module | What it does |
|-------|--------|--------------|
| **1 – Detect** | `runner.py` | Runs ALL tests N times (default 10). Flags any test that flips pass/fail as flaky. `pytest-json-report` for reliable parsing. |

- Static hints are **advisory only** — re-run is always the detection truth.
- Bob called via **subprocess**, one per flaky test, all **in parallel**.

- Patch kept **only on 50/50**; otherwise file is auto-reverted.

3 | ## Goal
4 | A one-day CLI tool that finds flaky tests in a Python/pytest project, diagnoses them, auto-patches them via IBM Bob, and proves the fix. Outputs a Markdown report, an HTML report, and per-patch `.diff` files.
5 | 
6 | ---
7 | 
8 | ## Project Structure
9 | 
10 | ```
11 | FlakeHunter/
12 | ├── demo_app/
13 | │   ├── app.py                  # tiny sample app (counter, fetch, random picker)
14 | │   └── tests/
15 | │       ├── test_stable.py      # ~8-10 always-passing tests
16 | │       ├── test_flaky_sleep.py # flaky: timing / time.sleep race

19 | │       └── test_flaky_state.py # flaky: shared global/module-level state

25 | │   ├── scanner.py              # static hint scanner (AST walk, ~50 lines)
26 | │   ├── diagnoser.py            # parallel Bob subprocesses, one per flaky test
27 | │   ├── patcher.py              # apply patch, verify 50/50, revert or keep
28 | │   └── reporter.py             # Markdown + self-contained HTML report
29 | │
30 | ├── reports/                    # created at runtime
31 | │   ├── report.md
32 | │   ├── report.html
33 | │   └── <test_name>.diff        # one per attempted patch
34 | │
35 | ├── requirements.txt
36 | ├── pyproject.toml              # [project.scripts] flakehunter = "flakehunter.cli:main"
37 | └── PLAN.md                     # this file
38 | ```
39 | 
40 | ---
41 | 
42 | ## Part 1 — demo_app/
43 | 
44 | ### `app.py`
45 | Three tiny functions used by the tests:
46 | - `increment(counter_dict)` — mutates a shared dict (enables shared-state flakiness)
47 | - `random_winner(items)` — returns `random.choice(items)` (no seed)
48 | - `fetch_status(url)` — does a real `urllib.request.urlopen(url).status` call
49 | 
50 | ### `tests/test_stable.py` (~8-10 tests)
51 | Pure, deterministic tests: arithmetic, string ops, list ops, dict ops. Always pass. Exist to prove FlakeHunter doesn't false-positive on good tests.
52 | 
53 | ### `tests/test_flaky_sleep.py` (1 test)
54 | Hint category: **timing**
55 | ```python
56 | # Records a start time, sleeps a variable amount, asserts elapsed < threshold.
57 | # Flaky because the sleep can overrun on a loaded CI machine.
58 | ```
59 | 
60 | ### `tests/test_flaky_random.py` (1 test)
61 | Hint category: **random**
62 | ```python
63 | # Calls random_winner() and asserts a specific element is returned.
64 | # Flaky because no seed is set.
65 | ```
66 | 
67 | ### `tests/test_flaky_network.py` (1 test)
68 | Hint category: **network**
69 | ```python
70 | # Calls fetch_status("http://httpbin.org/status/200") and asserts status == 200.
71 | # Flaky because the network may be down or the host may be slow.
72 | ```
73 | 
74 | ### `tests/test_flaky_state.py` (1 test)
75 | Hint category: **shared-state**
76 | ```python
77 | # Imports a module-level counter dict and calls increment() without resetting it.
78 | # Flaky when pytest re-uses the module across parametrize or re-runs.
79 | ```
80 | 
81 | ---
82 | 
83 | ## Part 2 — flakehunter/
84 | 
85 | ### `cli.py` — Click CLI
86 | ```
87 | flakehunter run <project_path>
88 |   --runs        N      # how many re-run passes (default: 10)
89 |   --workers     W      # parallel Bob subprocesses (default: 4)
90 |   --max-cost    $      # per-Bob-call cost cap forwarded to bob --max-cost
91 |   --dry-run            # skip Bob calls; report hints only, no patches
92 |   --output      DIR    # where to write reports/ (default: ./reports)
93 | ```
94 | Orchestrates the four phases in order: detect → hint → diagnose → patch → report.
95 | 
96 | ---
97 | 
98 | ### Phase 1 — `runner.py` — Re-run Detection
99 | 
100 | **Algorithm:**
101 | 1. Run `pytest <project_path> --tb=no -q` as a subprocess **N times** (default 10).
102 | 2. Collect pass/fail outcome per test node ID on each run (parse `pytest --json-report` or `-v` output).
103 | 3. A test is **flaky** if it has at least one PASS and at least one FAIL across the N runs.
104 | 4. Return a list of `FlakySummary(node_id, pass_count, fail_count)`.
105 | 
106 | **Key decisions:**
107 | - Use `pytest-json-report` plugin (add to `requirements.txt`) for reliable machine-readable output.
108 | - Runs are sequential (not parallel) to avoid shared-state tests masking each other.
109 | - All tests are always run — static hints never filter or skip a test.
110 | 
111 | ---
112 | 
113 | ### Phase 2 — `scanner.py` — Static Hint Scanner
114 | 
115 | **Algorithm:**
116 | 1. For each flaky `node_id`, resolve the source file path.
117 | 2. `ast.parse()` the file and walk all nodes.
118 | 3. Attach hint labels if any of these patterns appear **anywhere in the file**:
119 | 
120 | | Hint label      | AST pattern to detect                                      |
121 | |-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
122 | | `timing`        | `time.sleep(...)` call or `import time`                    |
123 | | `random`        | `random.*` call or `import random`                         |
124 | | `network`       | `urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, `socket`, `http` import     |
125 | | `shared-state`  | module-level mutable assignment (list/dict literal at top) |
126 | 
127 | 4. Return `hints: list[str]` per flaky test (may be empty — that's fine).
128 | 5. **Hints are advisory only.** They are injected into the Bob prompt to give context. They never gate or skip a test.
129 | 
130 | **Constraint:** This module should stay under ~60 lines. No external deps.
131 | 
132 | ---
133 | 
134 | ### Phase 3 — `diagnoser.py` — Bob-Powered Diagnosis & Patch Generation
135 | 
136 | **Algorithm:**
137 | 1. Build one prompt per flaky test:
138 |    ```
139 |    You are fixing a flaky pytest test.
140 |    Test: <node_id>
141 |    File: <source_file>
142 |    Hints: <hint labels from scanner>
143 |    Pass rate: <X>/N runs
144 | 
145 |    Read the test file and the app code it imports.
146 |    Produce a minimal unified diff that makes the test deterministic.
147 |    Output ONLY the unified diff, nothing else.
148 |    ```
149 | 2. Spawn one `bob run "<prompt>" --workspace <project_path> --format json --trust --accept-license --max-cost <limit>` subprocess **per flaky test**, all in **parallel** using `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor` (or `ThreadPoolExecutor` with subprocess).
150 | 3. Collect stdout from each Bob process. Parse the JSON response to extract the diff text.
151 | 4. If `--dry-run` is set, skip all Bob calls and return `None` diff for every test.
152 | 5. Return a list of `DiagnosisResult(node_id, diff_text | None, bob_raw_output)`.
153 | 
154 | ---
155 | 
156 | ### Phase 4 — `patcher.py` — Apply, Verify 50/50, Revert or Keep
157 | 
158 | For each `DiagnosisResult` with a non-None diff:
159 | 
160 | 1. **Save the diff** to `reports/<sanitized_node_id>.diff` unconditionally.
161 | 2. **Apply the patch** using Python's `subprocess.run(["patch", "-p1"], input=diff_text)` against the project path.
162 | 3. **Verify**: run `pytest <node_id>` exactly **50 times** sequentially.
163 | 4. **Decision:**
164 |    - If all 50 runs pass → **keep the patch**. Record `status=fixed`.
165 |    - If any run fails → **revert**: run `patch -p1 -R` to undo the change. Record `status=suggestion_only`.
166 | 5. Return a list of `PatchResult(node_id, status, diff_path)`.
167 | 
168 | **Safety rule:** The original file is always restored on revert. If `patch` itself fails to apply, record `status=patch_failed` and skip verification.
169 | 
170 | ---
171 | 
172 | ### Phase 5 — `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML Report
173 | 
174 | Generates two files in `<output>/`:
175 | 
176 | #### `report.md` structure:
177 | ```markdown
178 | # FlakeHunter Report
179 | Generated: <timestamp>  Project: <path>  Runs: N
180 | 
181 | ## Summary
182 | | Test | Pass | Fail | Hints | Outcome |
183 | |------|------|------|-------|---------|
184 | | ...  |  8   |  2   | timing, random | ✅ fixed |
185 | 
186 | ## Details
187 | ### <test_node_id>
188 | - **Hints:** timing
189 | - **Outcome:** fixed
190 | - **Diff:** [view patch](test_name.diff)
191 | ...
192 | ```
193 | 
194 | #### `report.html`
195 | - Single self-contained `.html` file (inline CSS, no external dependencies).
196 | - Same content as the Markdown report but rendered as an HTML table.
197 | - Color-coded rows: green = fixed, yellow = suggestion_only, red = patch_failed, grey = no diff (dry-run).
198 | - Each row has a collapsible `<details>` block showing the raw diff inline.
199 |

Runs on Windows (no `patch` binary required). --- ## Project Structure ``` FlakeHunter/ ├── demo_app/ │ ├── app.py # tiny sample app (counter, fake-network, random picker) │ └── tests/ │ ├── test_stable.py # ~8-10 always-passing tests │ ├── test_flaky_sleep.py # flaky: timing / time.sleep race │ ├── test_flaky_random.py # flaky: random without seed │ ├── test_flaky_network.py # flaky: simulated ~30% timeout (no real internet) │ └── test_flaky_state.py # flaky: two tests share module-level state, order-dependent │ ├── flakehunter/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── cli.py # entry point — Click CLI │ ├── runner.py # re-run detection (subprocess pytest, N passes) │ ├── scanner.py # static hint scanner (AST walk, ~60 lines) │ ├── diagnoser.py # parallel Bob subprocesses (ThreadPoolExecutor) │ ├── patcher.py # difflib diff, backup/apply/verify-50/revert │ └── reporter.py # Markdown + self-contained HTML report │ ├── reports/ # created at runtime │ ├── report.md │ ├── report.html │ └── .diff # one per attempted patch │ ├── requirements.txt ├── pyproject.toml └── PLAN.md # this file ``` --- ## Part 1 — demo_app/ ### `app.py` Four functions used by the tests. No real network calls — everything is local. - `increment(counter_dict, key)` — mutates a shared dict in-place; used by state tests - `random_winner(items)` — returns `random.choice(items)` with no seed - `fake_fetch(url)` — simulates a flaky HTTP call: - calls `random.random()`; if result < 0.30 raises `TimeoutError("simulated timeout")` - otherwise returns `{"status": 200}` - This keeps the suite fully offline and controllable - `compute(x, y)` — pure arithmetic; used by stable tests ### `tests/test_stable.py` (~8-10 tests) Pure, deterministic tests: arithmetic, string ops, list slicing, dict access, type checks. Never fail. Exist to prove FlakeHunter doesn't false-positive on good tests. ### `tests/test_flaky_sleep.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `timing` Records `time.time()`, calls `time.sleep(random.uniform(0.0, 0.2))`, asserts elapsed < 0.1 s. Fails ~50% of runs by design. Sleeps are intentionally short (max 0.2 s) to keep the suite fast. **Target failure rate: ~30-40% of runs.** ### `tests/test_flaky_random.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `random` Calls `random_winner(["a", "b", "c"])` and asserts the result is `"a"`. Fails ~67% of runs. Seeding `random` is the correct fix. **Target failure rate: ~30-40% of runs** (adjust list size to tune). ### `tests/test_flaky_network.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `network` Calls `fake_fetch("http://example.com/api")` and asserts `result["status"] == 200`. `fake_fetch` raises `TimeoutError` ~30% of the time using `random.random()`. No real internet access needed — fully self-contained. **Target failure rate: ~30% of runs.** ### `tests/test_flaky_state.py` (2 tests in 1 file) **Hint category:** `shared-state` ``` COUNTER = {"value": 0} # module-level mutable state def test_state_increment(): increment(COUNTER, "value") # adds 1 assert COUNTER["value"] == 1 # passes only if run first def test_state_reset(): assert COUNTER["value"] == 0 # passes only if run first ``` With `pytest-randomly` changing test order each run, one of the two tests will fail depending on execution order. **Target failure rate: ~30-40% of runs** (roughly when `test_state_reset` runs after `test_state_increment`). **`pytest-randomly`** is added to `requirements.txt`. It randomises test collection order on every run automatically. --- ## Part 2 — flakehunter/ ### `cli.py` — Click CLI ``` flakehunter run --runs N # re-run passes for detection (default: 20) --workers W # parallel Bob subprocesses (default: 4) --max-cost $ # per-Bob-call cost cap forwarded to bob --max-cost --dry-run # skip Bob calls; report hints only, no patches --output DIR # where to write reports (default: ./reports) flakehunter reset-demo # Restores demo_app/tests/ to their original flaky state. # Copies files from demo_app/tests/_originals/ back over demo_app/tests/. # Allows re-recording the demo without a git checkout. ``` Orchestrates phases in order: detect → hint → diagnose → patch → report. --- ### Phase 1 — `runner.py` — Re-run Detection **Algorithm:** 1. Run `pytest --tb=no -q --json-report --json-report-file=` as a subprocess **N times** (default 20). 2. Collect pass/fail outcome per test node ID on each run by reading the JSON report. 3. A test is **flaky** if it has ≥1 PASS **and** ≥1 FAIL across the N runs. 4. Return a list of `FlakySummary(node_id, pass_count, fail_count)`. **Key decisions:** - Use `pytest-json-report` for reliable machine-readable output. - Each run also passes `-p randomly --randomly-seed=random` so order varies. - Runs are **sequential** to avoid inter-test interference masking flakiness. - All tests are always run — static hints never filter or skip a test. - After all N runs, also compute **full-suite pass rate before patching** (stored for the report header). --- ### Phase 2 — `scanner.py` — Static Hint Scanner **Algorithm:** 1. For each flaky `node_id`, resolve its source file path from the node ID string. 2. `ast.parse()` the file and walk all nodes. 3. Attach hint labels for patterns found **anywhere in the file**: | Hint label | AST pattern to detect | |----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------| | `timing` | `time.sleep(...)` call or `import time` | | `random` | `random.*` call or `import random` | | `network` | import of `urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, `socket`, or `http` | | `shared-state` | module-level name assigned a `list` or `dict` literal | 4. Return `hints: list[str]` per flaky test (empty list is valid). 5. **Hints are advisory only** — injected into the Bob prompt as context clues. They never gate, skip, or filter a test. **Constraint:** ≤60 lines, stdlib only. --- ### Phase 3 — `diagnoser.py` — Bob-Powered Diagnosis & Patch (Windows-safe) #### Workspace isolation Each parallel Bob invocation gets its **own temporary copy** of the project: ``` tempfile.mkdtemp() → /tmp/flakehunter_/ shutil.copytree(project_path, temp_workspace) ``` Bob edits files **inside** the temp workspace. The real project is never touched during diagnosis. After Bob finishes, `diagnoser.py` collects the diff (see below) and deletes the temp dir. #### Bob invocation Resolve the Bob executable once at startup: ```python BOB_EXE = shutil.which("bob") or shutil.which("bob.cmd") ``` Then call, one subprocess per flaky test, all in **parallel** via `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers)`: ``` bob run "" \ --workspace \ --format json \ --trust \ --accept-license \ --max-cost ``` #### Bob prompt (structured JSON response requested) ``` You are fixing a flaky pytest test. Work entirely inside the workspace provided. Test node: Test file: Hints: Pass rate: / runs Read the test file and the app source it imports. Fix the test (or the app source) so the test becomes deterministic. Edit the files directly in the workspace. After editing, respond with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fences): { "root_cause": "", "explanation": "", "files_changed": ["", ""] } ``` #### Bob output parsing **Before writing the parser, run one live `bob run --format json` test** to inspect real stdout shape. The parser must handle: - JSON response from Bob containing the structured payload above. - Bob may wrap output in a `result` or `content` field — inspect first and code against the real shape. - If `--dry-run` is set, skip all Bob calls; return `DiagnosisResult` with `diff_text=None`, `root_cause="dry-run"`, `explanation=""`. #### Diff computation (no `patch` binary needed) After Bob edits files in the temp workspace: 1. For each path in `files_changed`, compare `original file` (from project) vs `edited file` (from temp workspace) using `difflib.unified_diff()`. 2. Concatenate all per-file diffs into one unified diff string. 3. Save to `reports/.diff` unconditionally. 4. Return `DiagnosisResult(node_id, diff_text, root_cause, explanation, files_changed)`. --- ### Phase 4 — `patcher.py` — Apply, Verify 50/50, Revert or Keep (Windows-safe) No `patch` binary used anywhere. All file operations are pure Python. **For each `DiagnosisResult` with non-None `diff_text`:** 1. **Backup originals:** ```python backups = {} for rel_path in result.files_changed: backups[rel_path] = Path(project / rel_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8") ``` 2. **Apply patch** by copying changed files from the temp workspace into the real project: ```python for rel_path in result.files_changed: shutil.copy(temp_workspace / rel_path, project / rel_path) ``` If any copy fails → record `status=patch_failed`, restore backups, skip verification. 3. **Verify:** run `pytest --tb=no -q --json-report` exactly **50 times** with `pytest-randomly` active (so test order varies each verification run). - Count passes and failures. 4. **Decision:** - All 50 pass → **keep the patch**. `status=fixed`. - Any failure → **revert**: write `backups[rel_path]` back to disk for every changed file. `status=suggestion_only`. 5. Return `PatchResult(node_id, status, diff_path, root_cause, explanation)`. **After all patches are evaluated**, compute **full-suite pass rate after patching** (stored for the report header). --- ### Phase 5 — `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML Report Generates two files in `/`. #### Report header fields ``` Generated: Project: Detection runs: N Flaky tests found: X → after patching: Y Full-suite pass rate: A% → after patching: B% Estimated developer time saved: ~Z hours (4 hrs per fixed test, 1 hr per suggestion) ``` #### `report.md` structure: ```markdown # FlakeHunter Report ...header fields... ## Summary | Test | Pass/N | Fail/N | Hints | Root Cause | Outcome | |------|--------|--------|-------|------------|---------| | ... | 16/20 | 4/20 | timing | timing | ✅ fixed | ## Details ### - **Hints:** timing - **Root cause:** timing - **Explanation:** The sleep duration is random and can exceed the assertion threshold on a loaded machine. The fix seeds the sleep to a fixed value so it is always deterministic. - **Outcome:** fixed - **Diff:** [view patch](test_name.diff) ``` #### `report.html` - Single self-contained `.html` file — inline CSS, zero external dependencies. - Same content rendered as styled HTML table. - Color-coded rows: 🟢 green = `fixed`, 🟡 yellow = `suggestion_only`, 🔴 red = `patch_failed`, ⚪ grey = no diff / dry-run. - Each row has a collapsible `
Show diff
...
` block with the raw diff inline. - Report header block at the top with before/after stats and estimated time saved. --- ## Data Flow ``` cli.py │ ├─► runner.py → list[FlakySummary] + before_pass_rate │ ├─► scanner.py → dict[node_id → list[str]] (hints) │ ├─► diagnoser.py → list[DiagnosisResult] │ ├── per test: mkdtemp → copytree → bob subprocess → parse JSON → difflib diff │ └── all tests run in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor │ ├─► patcher.py → list[PatchResult] + after_pass_rate │ ├── backup originals │ ├── apply by file copy (no patch binary) │ ├── verify 50x with pytest-randomly │ └── revert if any failure (restore backups) │ └─► reporter.py → reports/report.md reports/report.html reports/.diff ``` --- ## `requirements.txt` ``` click>=8.1 pytest>=7.0 pytest-json-report>=1.5 pytest-randomly>=3.12 ``` No binary dependencies. Works on Windows, macOS, Linux. --- ## `pyproject.toml` (minimal) ```toml [project] name = "flakehunter" version = "0.1.0" requires-python = ">=3.10" dependencies = [ "click>=8.1", "pytest>=7.0", "pytest-json-report>=1.5", "pytest-randomly>=3.12", ] [project.scripts] flakehunter = "flakehunter.cli:main" [build-system] requires = ["setuptools"] build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta" ``` --- ## `reset-demo` command `flakehunter reset-demo` restores the demo suite to its original flaky state so the demo can be re-recorded without a git checkout. **Implementation:** - At scaffold time, copy the original flaky test files into `demo_app/tests/_originals/`. - `reset-demo` iterates `_originals/` and copies each file back to `demo_app/tests/`. - Prints "Demo reset to original flaky state." on success. --- ## Bob Output Parser — Pre-flight Step **Before implementing the JSON parser**, run this one-off command in a terminal and capture real stdout: ``` bob run "Hello, respond with JSON: {\"status\": \"ok\"}" --format json --trust --accept-license ``` Inspect the structure (top-level keys, nesting, how content is embedded). Code the parser in `diagnoser.py` against the **actual** output shape, not an assumed shape. --- ## One-Day Build Order | # | Task | Est. | |---|------|------| | 1 | Scaffold folders, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt` | 15 min | | 2 | Write `demo_app/app.py` + all 5 test files + `_originals/` | 35 min | | 3 | `runner.py` — re-run detection loop + before_pass_rate | 45 min | | 4 | `scanner.py` — AST hint scanner | 30 min | | 5 | `cli.py` — Click wiring (`run` + `reset-demo`), `--dry-run` flag | 30 min | | 6 | Pre-flight: run `bob run --format json` and inspect output shape | 15 min | | 7 | `diagnoser.py` — temp workspace isolation, Bob subprocess, JSON parser, difflib diff, ThreadPoolExecutor | 75 min | | 8 | `patcher.py` — backup/apply-by-copy/verify-50x/revert loop + after_pass_rate | 50 min | | 9 | `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML (header stats, root cause, explanation, diff blocks) | 50 min | |10 | End-to-end smoke test with `--dry-run` | 20 min | |11 | End-to-end test with real Bob (credits) | 30 min | | **Total** | | **~6.5 hr** | --- ## Key Design Constraints (do not drift from these) - **Static hints are advisory only** — re-run detection is always the source of truth for flakiness. - **No `patch` binary** — apply changes by file copy (Python only). Revert by restoring in-memory backups. - **Workspace isolation** — each parallel Bob call gets its own `tempfile.mkdtemp()` copy of the project; the real project is never touched during diagnosis. - **Bob executable** resolved via `shutil.which("bob") or shutil.which("bob.cmd")`. - **ThreadPoolExecutor** for parallelism (not ProcessPoolExecutor) — subprocesses are already the unit of work. - **`--dry-run`** skips ALL Bob calls; detect + hint + report still run normally. - **50/50 verification** uses `pytest-randomly` so test order varies on every verification pass. - Patch kept **only on 50/50**; otherwise file is auto-reverted from in-memory backup. - Every attempted diff saved to `reports/.diff` regardless of outcome. - **HTML report is fully self-contained** — no CDN, no external CSS or JS. - **Pre-flight Bob output inspection** is a mandatory step before writing the JSON parser. - **`flakehunter reset-demo`** restores originals from `demo_app/tests/_originals/`, no git required. - All flaky tests target **~30-40% failure rate** at N=20 runs. Sleeps ≤ 0.2 s. No real internet.

# FlakeHunter — Hackathon Plan (v2) ## Goal A one-day CLI tool that finds flaky tests in a Python/pytest project, diagnoses them, auto-patches them via IBM Bob (agent mode), and proves the fix. Outputs a Markdown report, an HTML report, and per-patch `.diff` files. Runs on Windows (no `patch` binary required). --- ## Project Structure ``` FlakeHunter/ ├── demo_app/ │ ├── app.py # tiny sample app (counter, fake-network, random picker) │ └── tests/ │ ├── test_stable.py # ~8-10 always-passing tests │ ├── test_flaky_sleep.py # flaky: timing / time.sleep race │ ├── test_flaky_random.py # flaky: random without seed │ ├── test_flaky_network.py # flaky: simulated ~30% timeout (no real internet) │ └── test_flaky_state.py # flaky: two tests share module-level state, order-dependent │ ├── flakehunter/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── cli.py # entry point — Click CLI │ ├── runner.py # re-run detection (subprocess pytest, N passes) │ ├── scanner.py # static hint scanner (AST walk, ~60 lines) │ ├── diagnoser.py # parallel Bob subprocesses (ThreadPoolExecutor) │ ├── patcher.py # difflib diff, backup/apply/verify-50/revert │ └── reporter.py # Markdown + self-contained HTML report │ ├── reports/ # created at runtime │ ├── report.md │ ├── report.html │ └── .diff # one per attempted patch │ ├── requirements.txt ├── pyproject.toml └── PLAN.md # this file ``` --- ## Part 1 — demo_app/ ### `app.py` Four functions used by the tests. No real network calls — everything is local. - `increment(counter_dict, key)` — mutates a shared dict in-place; used by state tests - `random_winner(items)` — returns `random.choice(items)` with no seed - `fake_fetch(url)` — simulates a flaky HTTP call: - calls `random.random()`; if result < 0.30 raises `TimeoutError("simulated timeout")` - otherwise returns `{"status": 200}` - This keeps the suite fully offline and controllable - `compute(x, y)` — pure arithmetic; used by stable tests ### `tests/test_stable.py` (~8-10 tests) Pure, deterministic tests: arithmetic, string ops, list slicing, dict access, type checks. Never fail. Exist to prove FlakeHunter doesn't false-positive on good tests. ### `tests/test_flaky_sleep.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `timing` Records `time.time()`, calls `time.sleep(random.uniform(0.0, 0.2))`, asserts elapsed < 0.1 s. Fails ~50% of runs by design. Sleeps are intentionally short (max 0.2 s) to keep the suite fast. **Target failure rate: ~30-40% of runs.** ### `tests/test_flaky_random.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `random` Calls `random_winner(["a", "b", "c"])` and asserts the result is `"a"`. Fails ~67% of runs. Seeding `random` is the correct fix. **Target failure rate: ~30-40% of runs** (adjust list size to tune). ### `tests/test_flaky_network.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `network` Calls `fake_fetch("http://example.com/api")` and asserts `result["status"] == 200`. `fake_fetch` raises `TimeoutError` ~30% of the time using `random.random()`. No real internet access needed — fully self-contained. **Target failure rate: ~30% of runs.** ### `tests/test_flaky_state.py` (2 tests in 1 file) **Hint category:** `shared-state` ``` COUNTER = {"value": 0} # module-level mutable state def test_state_increment(): increment(COUNTER, "value") # adds 1 assert COUNTER["value"] == 1 # passes only if run first def test_state_reset(): assert COUNTER["value"] == 0 # passes only if run first ``` With `pytest-randomly` changing test order each run, one of the two tests will fail depending on execution order. **Target failure rate: ~30-40% of runs** (roughly when `test_state_reset` runs after `test_state_increment`). **`pytest-randomly`** is added to `requirements.txt`. It randomises test collection order on every run automatically. --- ## Part 2 — flakehunter/ ### `cli.py` — Click CLI ``` flakehunter run --runs N # re-run passes for detection (default: 20) --workers W # parallel Bob subprocesses (default: 4) --max-cost $ # per-Bob-call cost cap forwarded to bob --max-cost --dry-run # skip Bob calls; report hints only, no patches --output DIR # where to write reports (default: ./reports) flakehunter reset-demo # Restores demo_app/tests/ to their original flaky state. # Copies files from demo_app/tests/_originals/ back over demo_app/tests/. # Allows re-recording the demo without a git checkout. ``` Orchestrates phases in order: detect → hint → diagnose → patch → report. --- ### Phase 1 — `runner.py` — Re-run Detection **Algorithm:** 1. Run `pytest --tb=no -q --json-report --json-report-file=` as a subprocess **N times** (default 20). 2. Collect pass/fail outcome per test node ID on each run by reading the JSON report. 3. A test is **flaky** if it has ≥1 PASS **and** ≥1 FAIL across the N runs. 4. Return a list of `FlakySummary(node_id, pass_count, fail_count)`. **Key decisions:** - Use `pytest-json-report` for reliable machine-readable output. - Each run also passes `-p randomly --randomly-seed=random` so order varies. - Runs are **sequential** to avoid inter-test interference masking flakiness. - All tests are always run — static hints never filter or skip a test. - After all N runs, also compute **full-suite pass rate before patching** (stored for the report header). --- ### Phase 2 — `scanner.py` — Static Hint Scanner **Algorithm:** 1. For each path in `files_changed`, compare `original file` (from project) vs `edited file` (from temp workspace) using `difflib.unified_diff()`. 2. Concatenate all per-file diffs into one unified diff string. 3. Save to `reports/.diff` unconditionally. 4. Return `DiagnosisResult(node_id, diff_text, root_cause, explanation, files_changed)`. --- ### Phase 4 — `patcher.py` — Apply, Verify 50/50, Revert or Keep (Windows-safe) No `patch` binary used anywhere. All file operations are pure Python. **For each `DiagnosisResult` with non-None `diff_text`:** 1. **Backup originals:** ```python backups = {} for rel_path in result.files_changed: backups[rel_path] = Path(project / rel_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8") ``` 2. **Apply patch** by copying changed files from the temp workspace into the real project: ```python for rel_path in result.files_changed: shutil.copy(temp_workspace / rel_path, project / rel_path) ``` If any copy fails → record `status=patch_failed`, restore backups, skip verification. 3. **Verify:** run `pytest --tb=no -q --json-report` exactly **50 times** with `pytest-randomly` active (so test order varies each verification run). - Count passes and failures. 4. **Decision:** - All 50 pass → **keep the patch**. `status=fixed`. - Any failure → **revert**: write `backups[rel_path]` back to disk for every changed file. `status=suggestion_only`. 5. Return `PatchResult(node_id, status, diff_path, root_cause, explanation)`. **After all patches are evaluated**, compute **full-suite pass rate after patching** (stored for the report header). --- ### Phase 5 — `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML Report Generates two files in `/`. #### Report header fields ``` Generated: Project: Detection runs: N Flaky tests found: X → after patching: Y Full-suite pass rate: A% → after patching: B% Estimated developer time saved: ~Z hours (4 hrs per fixed test, 1 hr per suggestion) ``` #### `report.md` structure: ```markdown # FlakeHunter Report ...header fields... ## Summary | Test | Pass/N | Fail/N | Hints | Root Cause | Outcome | |------|--------|--------|-------|------------|---------| | ... | 16/20 | 4/20 | timing | timing | ✅ fixed | ## Details ### - **Hints:** timing - **Root cause:** timing - **Explanation:** The sleep duration is random and can exceed the assertion threshold on a loaded machine. ## Part 2 — flakehunter/

### `cli.py` — Click CLI
```
flakehunter run <project_path>
  --runs        N      # how many re-run passes (default: 10)
  --workers     W      # parallel Bob subprocesses (default: 4)
  --max-cost    $      # per-Bob-call cost cap forwarded to bob --max-cost
  --dry-run            # skip Bob calls; report hints only, no patches
  --output      DIR    # where to write reports/ (default: ./reports)
```
Orchestrates the four phases in order: detect → hint → diagnose → patch → report.

---

### Phase 1 — `runner.py` — Re-run Detection

**Algorithm:**
1. Run `pytest <project_path> --tb=no -q` as a subprocess **N times** (default 10).
2. Collect pass/fail outcome per test node ID on each run (parse `pytest --json-report` or `-v` output).
3. A test is **flaky** if it has at least one PASS and at least one FAIL across the N runs.
4. Return a list of `FlakySummary(node_id, pass_count, fail_count)`.

**Key decisions:**
- Use `pytest-json-report` plugin (add to `requirements.txt`) for reliable machine-readable output.
- Runs are sequential (not parallel) to avoid shared-state tests masking each other.
- All tests are always run — static hints never filter or skip a test.

---

### Phase 2 — `scanner.py` — Static Hint Scanner

**Algorithm:**
1. For each flaky `node_id`, resolve the source file path.
2. `ast.parse()` the file and walk all nodes.
3. Attach hint labels if any of these patterns appear **anywhere in the file**:

| Hint label      | AST pattern to detect                                      |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `timing`        | `time.sleep(...)` call or `import time`                    |
| `random`        | `random.*` call or `import random`                         |
| `network`       | `urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, `socket`, `http` import     |
| `shared-state`  | module-level mutable assignment (list/dict literal at top) |

4. Return `hints: list[str]` per flaky test (may be empty — that's fine).
5. **Hints are advisory only.** They are injected into the Bob prompt to give context. They never gate or skip a test.

**Constraint:** This module should stay under ~60 lines. No external deps.

---

### Phase 3 — `diagnoser.py` — Bob-Powered Diagnosis & Patch Generation

**Algorithm:**
1. Build one prompt per flaky test:
   ```
   You are fixing a flaky pytest test.
   Test: <node_id>
   File: <source_file>
   Hints: <hint labels from scanner>
   Pass rate: <X>/N runs

   Read the test file and the app code it imports.
   Produce a minimal unified diff that makes the test deterministic.
   Output ONLY the unified diff, nothing else.
   ```
2. Spawn one `bob run "<prompt>" --workspace <project_path> --format json --trust --accept-license --max-cost <limit>` subprocess **per flaky test**, all in **parallel** using `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor` (or `ThreadPoolExecutor` with subprocess).
3. Collect stdout from each Bob process. Parse the JSON response to extract the diff text.
4. If `--dry-run` is set, skip all Bob calls and return `None` diff for every test.
5. Return a list of `DiagnosisResult(node_id, diff_text | None, bob_raw_output)`.

---

### Phase 4 — `patcher.py` — Apply, Verify 50/50, Revert or Keep

For each `DiagnosisResult` with a non-None diff:

1. **Save the diff** to `reports/<sanitized_node_id>.diff` unconditionally.
2. **Apply the patch** using Python's `subprocess.run(["patch", "-p1"], input=diff_text)` against the project path.
3. **Verify**: run `pytest <node_id>` exactly **50 times** sequentially.
4. **Decision:**
   - If all 50 runs pass → **keep the patch**. Record `status=fixed`.
   - If any run fails → **revert**: run `patch -p1 -R` to undo the change. Record `status=suggestion_only`.
5. Return a list of `PatchResult(node_id, status, diff_path)`.

**Safety rule:** The original file is always restored on revert. If `patch` itself fails to apply, record `status=patch_failed` and skip verification.

---

### Phase 5 — `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML Report

Generates two files in `<output>/`:

#### `report.md` structure:
```markdown
# FlakeHunter Report
Generated: <timestamp>  Project: <path>  Runs: N

## Summary
| Test | Pass | Fail | Hints | Outcome |
|------|------|------|-------|---------|
| ...  |  8   |  2   | timing, random | ✅ fixed |

## Details
### <test_node_id>
- **Hints:** timing
- **Outcome:** fixed
- **Diff:** [view patch](test_name.diff)
...
```

#### `report.html`
- Single self-contained `.html` file (inline CSS, no external dependencies).
- Same content as the Markdown report but rendered as an HTML table.
- Color-coded rows: green = fixed, yellow = suggestion_only, red = patch_failed, grey = no diff (dry-run).
- Each row has a collapsible `<details>` block showing the raw diff inline.

---

cli.py

## Key Design Constraints (do not drift from these)

- Static hints **never** gate or skip any test — re-run is always the detection source of truth.
- Bob is called via **subprocess** (`bob run "..." --workspace ... --format json --trust --accept-license --max-cost ...`), one process per flaky test, all in parallel.
- `--dry-run` skips ALL Bob calls; the rest of the pipeline (detect, hint, report) still runs.
- A patch is kept **only if it passes 50/50 sequential re-runs**; otherwise the file is auto-reverted.
- Every attempted diff is saved to `reports/<test>.diff` regardless of outcome.
- HTML report is **self-contained** (no CDN links, no external CSS).

# FlakeHunter — Hackathon Plan (v3) ## Goal A one-day CLI tool that finds flaky tests in a Python/pytest project, diagnoses them, auto-patches them via IBM Bob (agent mode), and proves the fix. Outputs a Markdown report, an HTML report, and per-patch `.diff` files. Runs on Windows (no `patch` binary required). --- ## Project Structure ``` FlakeHunter/ ├── demo_app/ │ ├── app.py # tiny sample app (counter, fake-network, random picker) │ └── tests/ │ ├── test_stable.py # ~8-10 always-passing tests │ ├── test_flaky_sleep.py # flaky: timing / time.sleep race │ ├── test_flaky_random.py # flaky: random without seed │ ├── test_flaky_network.py # flaky: simulated ~30% timeout (no real internet) │ └── test_flaky_state.py # flaky: two tests share module-level state, order-dependent │ ├── demo_originals/ # git-committed snapshot of the flaky demo (never collected by pytest) │ ├── app.py # original flaky app.py │ └── tests/ │ ├── test_stable.py │ ├── test_flaky_sleep.py │ ├── test_flaky_random.py │ ├── test_flaky_network.py │ └── test_flaky_state.py │ ├── flakehunter/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── cli.py # entry point — Click CLI │ ├── runner.py # re-run detection (subprocess pytest, N passes) │ ├── scanner.py # static hint scanner (AST walk, ≤60 lines) │ ├── diagnoser.py # parallel Bob subprocesses (ThreadPoolExecutor) │ ├── patcher.py # difflib diff, backup/apply/verify-50/revert │ └── reporter.py # Markdown + self-contained HTML report │ ├── reports/ # created at runtime │ ├── report.md │ ├── report.html │ └── .diff # one per attempted patch │ ├── requirements.txt ├── pyproject.toml └── PLAN.md # this file ``` --- ## Part 1 — demo_app/ ### `app.py` Four functions used by the tests. No real network calls — everything is local. - `increment(counter_dict, key)` — mutates a shared dict in-place; used by state tests - `random_winner(items)` — returns `random.choice(items)` with no seed - `fake_fetch(url)` — simulates a flaky HTTP call: - calls `random.random()`; if result < 0.30 raises `TimeoutError("simulated timeout")` - otherwise returns `{"status": 200}` - Fully offline and controllable - `compute(x, y)` — pure arithmetic; used by stable tests ### `tests/test_stable.py` (~8-10 tests) Pure, deterministic tests: arithmetic, string ops, list slicing, dict access, type checks. Never fail. Exist to prove FlakeHunter doesn't false-positive on good tests. ### `tests/test_flaky_sleep.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `timing` Records `time.time()`, calls `time.sleep(random.uniform(0.0, 0.15))`, asserts elapsed < 0.1 s. Fails ~33% of runs (when sleep lands in the 0.1–0.15 s range). **Target failure rate: ~33% of runs.** ### `tests/test_flaky_random.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `random` Calls `random_winner(["a", "b", "c"])` and asserts the result is **in `["a", "b"]`**. Fails ~33% of runs (when `"c"` is chosen). **Target failure rate: ~33% of runs.** ### `tests/test_flaky_network.py` (1 test) **Hint category:** `network` Calls `fake_fetch("http://example.com/api")` and asserts `result["status"] == 200`. `fake_fetch` raises `TimeoutError` ~30% of the time using `random.random()`. No real internet access needed — fully self-contained. **Target failure rate: ~30% of runs.** ### `tests/test_flaky_state.py` (2 tests in 1 file) **Hint category:** `shared-state` ```python COUNTER = {"value": 0} # module-level mutable state def test_state_increment(): increment(COUNTER, "value") # adds 1 assert COUNTER["value"] == 1 # passes only if run first def test_state_reset(): assert COUNTER["value"] == 0 # passes only if run first ``` With `pytest-randomly` changing test order each run, one of the two tests will fail depending on execution order. **Target failure rate: ~50% of runs** (fails whenever `test_state_reset` runs after `test_state_increment`). **`pytest-randomly`** is added to `requirements.txt`. It randomises test collection order automatically. --- ### `demo_originals/` — snapshot for `reset-demo` `demo_originals/` lives at the **project root** (not inside `demo_app/tests/`), so pytest **never collects it**. It contains an exact copy of the original flaky files at scaffold time: ``` demo_originals/ ├── app.py └── tests/ ├── test_stable.py ├── test_flaky_sleep.py ├── test_flaky_random.py ├── test_flaky_network.py └── test_flaky_state.py ``` `flakehunter reset-demo` copies these files back over `demo_app/app.py` and `demo_app/tests/*`, restoring the full flaky demo without a git checkout. Both `app.py` and all test files are restored. --- ## Part 2 — flakehunter/ ### `cli.py` — Click CLI ``` flakehunter run --runs N # re-run passes for detection (default: 20) --workers W # parallel Bob subprocesses (default: 4) --max-cost $ # per-Bob-call cost cap (default: 1.0) --dry-run # skip Bob calls; report hints only, no patches --output DIR # where to write reports (default: ./reports) --ci-runs-per-day N # for time-saved formula (default: 10) --minutes-per-rerun N# for time-saved formula (default: 5) flakehunter reset-demo # Copies demo_originals/app.py → demo_app/app.py # Copies demo_originals/tests/* → demo_app/tests/* # Prints "Demo reset to original flaky state." ``` Orchestrates phases in order: detect → hint → diagnose → patch → report. --- ### Phase 1 — `runner.py` — Re-run Detection **Algorithm:** 1. Run `pytest --tb=no -q --json-report --json-report-file=` as a subprocess **N times** (default 20). 2. Collect pass/fail outcome per test node ID on each run by reading the JSON report. 3. A test is **flaky** if it has ≥1 PASS **and** ≥1 FAIL across the N runs. 4. Return a list of `FlakySummary(node_id, pass_count, fail_count)`. **Key decisions:** - Use `pytest-json-report` for reliable machine-readable output. - `pytest-randomly` shuffles test order automatically on every run (no extra flag needed). - Runs are **sequential** to avoid inter-test interference masking flakiness. - All tests are always run — static hints never filter or skip a test. - After all N runs, compute **full-suite pass rate before patching** (stored for the report header). --- ### Phase 2 — `scanner.py` — Static Hint Scanner **Algorithm:** 1. For each flaky `node_id`, resolve its source file path from the node ID string. 2. `ast.parse()` the file and walk all nodes. 3. Attach hint labels for patterns found **anywhere in the file**: | Hint label | AST pattern to detect | |----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------| | `timing` | `time.sleep(...)` call or `import time` | | `random` | `random.*` call or `import random` | | `network` | import of `urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, `socket`, or `http` | | `shared-state` | module-level name assigned a `list` or `dict` literal | 4. Return `hints: list[str]` per flaky test (empty list is valid). 5. **Hints are advisory only** — injected into the Bob prompt as context clues. They never gate, skip, or filter a test. **Constraint:** ≤60 lines, stdlib only. --- ### Phase 3 — `diagnoser.py` — Bob-Powered Diagnosis & Patch (Windows-safe) #### Workspace isolation Each parallel Bob invocation gets its **own temporary copy** of the project: ```python tempfile.mkdtemp() → temp_workspace shutil.copytree( project_path, temp_workspace, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns( "__pycache__", ".pytest_cache", "reports", ".venv", ".git" ), dirs_exist_ok=True, ) ``` Bob edits files **inside** the temp workspace. The real project is never touched during diagnosis. After Bob finishes, `diagnoser.py` computes the diff and deletes the temp dir. #### Bob invocation Resolve the Bob executable once at startup: ```python BOB_EXE = shutil.which("bob") or shutil.which("bob.cmd") ``` Spawn one subprocess per flaky test, all in **parallel** via `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers)`: ``` bob run "" \ --workspace \ --format json \ --trust \ --accept-license \ --max-cost 1.0 ``` #### Bob prompt — test-file-only constraint Bob must **only edit the test file** for its assigned flaky test. `app.py` must never be modified. This prevents parallel Bob processes from overwriting each other's changes to shared app files. Fix strategy per category (in the prompt): - **timing**: use `unittest.mock.patch` or `monkeypatch` to control `time.sleep` in the test - **random**: seed `random` in the test or use `monkeypatch` to patch `random.choice` - **network**: mock `fake_fetch` via `monkeypatch` in the test so it never raises - **shared-state**: add a `setup_function` or fixture in the test file that resets the shared state before each test ``` You are fixing a flaky pytest test. Work entirely inside the workspace provided. You MUST only edit the test file listed below. Do NOT modify app.py or any other file. Test node: Test file: Hints: Pass rate: / runs Read the test file and the app source it imports (for context only — do not edit app.py). Fix the test so it becomes deterministic by editing ONLY the test file. Use monkeypatch, fixtures, or setup_function as needed. After editing, respond with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fences): { "root_cause": "", "explanation": "", "files_changed": [""] } ``` #### Bob output parsing **Before writing the parser, run one live `bob run --format json` test** to inspect real stdout shape. The parser must handle the actual JSON envelope Bob returns. Code against the real shape, not an assumed shape. If `--dry-run` is set, skip all Bob calls; return `DiagnosisResult` with `diff_text=None`, `root_cause="dry-run"`, `explanation=""`. #### Diff computation (no `patch` binary needed) After Bob edits files in the temp workspace: 1. For each path in `files_changed`, compare original file (from project) vs edited file (from temp workspace) using `difflib.unified_diff()`. 2. Concatenate all per-file diffs into one unified diff string. 3. Save to `reports/.diff` unconditionally. 4. Return `DiagnosisResult(node_id, diff_text, root_cause, explanation, files_changed)`. --- ### Phase 4 — `patcher.py` — Apply, Verify 50/50, Revert or Keep (Windows-safe) No `patch` binary used anywhere. All file operations are pure Python. **For each `DiagnosisResult` with non-None `diff_text`:** 1. **Backup originals:** ```python backups = {} for rel_path in result.files_changed: backups[rel_path] = Path(project / rel_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8") ``` 2. **Apply patch** by copying changed files from the temp workspace into the real project: ```python for rel_path in result.files_changed: shutil.copy(temp_workspace / rel_path, project / rel_path) ``` If any copy fails → record `status=patch_failed`, restore backups, skip verification. 3. **Verify:** Run the **entire test file** (not just the single node ID) 50 times sequentially with `pytest-randomly` active so order varies on every pass: ``` pytest --tb=no -q --json-report --json-report-file= ``` From each JSON report, extract the outcome of `` specifically. Count passes and failures for that node across all 50 runs. > **Why the whole file?** Order-dependent tests (shared-state category) can only be proven > fixed by running all tests in the file together so `pytest-randomly` can exercise all orderings. > Running a single node ID in isolation would always pass and give a false positive. 4. **Decision:** - All 50 passes for `` → **keep the patch**. `status=fixed`. - Any failure → **revert**: write `backups[rel_path]` back to disk for every changed file. `status=suggestion_only`. 5. Return `PatchResult(node_id, status, diff_path, root_cause, explanation)`. **After all patches are evaluated**, compute **full-suite pass rate after patching** (stored for the report header). --- ### Phase 5 — `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML Report Generates two files in `/`. #### Report header fields ``` Generated: Project: Detection runs: N Flaky tests found: X → after patching: Y remaining Full-suite pass rate: A% → after patching: B% Estimated developer time saved: ~Z hours Formula: (fixed_count × 4 h) + (suggestion_count × 1 h) Assumptions: 4 h to manually find+fix a flaky test; 1 h to apply a suggestion. Configurable via --ci-runs-per-day and --minutes-per-rerun (shown if provided). ``` If `--ci-runs-per-day` and `--minutes-per-rerun` are given, also show: ``` CI time saved per day: fixed_count × ci_runs_per_day × minutes_per_rerun minutes ``` #### `report.md` structure: ```markdown # FlakeHunter Report ...header fields... ## Summary | Test | Pass/N | Fail/N | Hints | Root Cause | Outcome | |------|--------|--------|-------|------------|---------| | ... | 14/20 | 6/20 | timing | timing | ✅ fixed | ## Details ### - **Hints:** timing - **Root cause:** timing - **Explanation:** The sleep duration is random and can exceed the assertion threshold. The fix patches time.sleep in the test using monkeypatch so the duration is always deterministic. - **Outcome:** fixed - **Diff:** [view patch](test_name.diff) ``` #### `report.html` - Single self-contained `.html` file — inline CSS, zero external dependencies. - Same content rendered as styled HTML table. - Color-coded rows: 🟢 green = `fixed`, 🟡 yellow = `suggestion_only`, 🔴 red = `patch_failed`, ⚪ grey = no diff / dry-run. - Each row has a collapsible `
Show diff
...
` block. - Report header block at the top with before/after stats, formula, and estimated time saved. --- ## Data Flow ``` cli.py │ ├─► runner.py → list[FlakySummary] + before_pass_rate │ ├─► scanner.py → dict[node_id → list[str]] (hints) │ ├─► diagnoser.py → list[DiagnosisResult] │ ├── per test: mkdtemp → copytree (ignore: __pycache__/.git/.venv/reports) │ │ → bob subprocess → parse JSON → difflib diff → rmtree │ └── all tests run in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor │ ├─► patcher.py → list[PatchResult] + after_pass_rate │ ├── backup originals (in-memory) │ ├── apply by file copy (no patch binary) │ ├── verify 50× by running WHOLE TEST FILE with pytest-randomly │ │ and tracking node_id outcome from JSON report │ └── revert if any failure (restore from in-memory backup) │ └─► reporter.py → reports/report.md reports/report.html reports/.diff ``` --- ## `requirements.txt` ``` click>=8.1 pytest>=7.0 pytest-json-report>=1.5 pytest-randomly>=3.12 ``` No binary dependencies. Works on Windows, macOS, Linux. --- ## `pyproject.toml` ```toml [project] name = "flakehunter" version = "0.1.0" requires-python = ">=3.10" dependencies = [ "click>=8.1", "pytest>=7.0", "pytest-json-report>=1.5", "pytest-randomly>=3.12", ] [project.scripts] flakehunter = "flakehunter.cli:main" [build-system] requires = ["setuptools"] build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta" ``` --- ## `reset-demo` command `flakehunter reset-demo` restores the demo to its original flaky state without a git checkout. **Implementation:** 1. Copy `demo_originals/app.py` → `demo_app/app.py` 2. Copy every file in `demo_originals/tests/` → `demo_app/tests/` 3. Print "Demo reset to original flaky state." `demo_originals/` is committed to git at scaffold time and never modified by FlakeHunter. Because it lives at the project root (not under `demo_app/tests/`), pytest never collects it. --- ## Bob Output Parser — Pre-flight Step **Before implementing the JSON parser**, run this one-off command and capture real stdout: ``` bob run "Hello, respond with JSON: {\"status\": \"ok\"}" --format json --trust --accept-license ``` Inspect the structure (top-level keys, nesting, how text content is embedded). Code the parser in `diagnoser.py` against the **actual** output shape, not an assumed shape. --- ## One-Day Build Order | # | Task | Est. | |---|------|------| | 1 | Scaffold folders, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `git init` + first commit | 20 min | | 2 | Write `demo_app/app.py` + all test files + `demo_originals/` snapshot | 35 min | | 3 | `runner.py` — re-run detection loop + `before_pass_rate` | 45 min | | 4 | `scanner.py` — AST hint scanner | 30 min | | 5 | `cli.py` — Click wiring (`run` + `reset-demo`), `--dry-run`, `--max-cost 1.0` default | 30 min | | 6 | Pre-flight: run `bob run --format json` and inspect output shape | 15 min | | 7 | `diagnoser.py` — temp workspace isolation (with ignore patterns), Bob subprocess, JSON parser, difflib diff, ThreadPoolExecutor | 75 min | | 8 | `patcher.py` — backup / apply-by-copy / verify-whole-file-50× / revert + `after_pass_rate` | 50 min | | 9 | `reporter.py` — Markdown + HTML (header stats, formula, root cause, explanation, diff blocks) | 50 min | |10 | End-to-end smoke test with `--dry-run` | 20 min | |11 | End-to-end test with real Bob (credits) | 30 min | | **Total** | | **~6.5 hr** | --- ## Key Design Constraints (do not drift from these) - **Static hints are advisory only** — re-run detection is always the source of truth for flakiness. - **No `patch` binary** — apply changes by file copy (Python only). Revert by restoring in-memory string backups. - **Workspace isolation** — each parallel Bob call gets its own `tempfile.mkdtemp()` copy of the project (with `shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", ".pytest_cache", "reports", ".venv", ".git")`). The real project is never touched during diagnosis. - **Bob edits only the test file** for its assigned test — never `app.py` or any other file. This is enforced by the prompt and verified by checking `files_changed`. - **Bob executable** resolved via `shutil.which("bob") or shutil.which("bob.cmd")`. - **ThreadPoolExecutor** for parallelism (not ProcessPoolExecutor) — subprocesses are already the unit of work. - **`--dry-run`** skips ALL Bob calls; detect + hint + report still run normally. - **Default `--max-cost 1.0`** per Bob call. - **Verification runs the whole test file 50×** (not just the single node ID) so order-dependent tests are exercised with varying orderings via `pytest-randomly`. The node ID's outcome is tracked from the JSON report. - Patch kept **only on 50/50**; otherwise file is auto-reverted from in-memory backup. - Every attempted diff saved to `reports/.diff` regardless of outcome. - **HTML report is fully self-contained** — no CDN, no external CSS or JS. - **Pre-flight Bob output inspection** is a mandatory step before writing the JSON parser. - **`demo_originals/`** lives at project root (never collected by pytest); **`reset-demo`** restores both `app.py` and all test files. - **`git init`** + first commit after scaffold (step 1 of build order). - Flaky test target failure rates: sleep ~33%, random ~33%, network ~30%, shared-state ~50%. Sleeps ≤ 0.15 s. No real internet. - Time-saved formula and assumptions are **explicit and shown in the report**. CI rate and minutes-per-rerun are configurable flags.
